## Introduction



## Introduction


Welcome to IGN’s Guide to survival in the  		  wide world of Norrath, otherwise known as EverQuest. Just in case you’ve  		  been living under a rock for the past year, EverQuest is a "Massively Multiplayer  		  Online Roleplaying" game developed by Verant Interactive. Players choose  		  from many different races, classes and religions and then set out to make  		  their own virtual life in the virtual fantasy realm of Norrath.

This guide will arrive in multiple parts, over  		  a series of months. Each part will detail what and where to fight at certain  		  levels to fill that experience bar of yours. Also, each section of the guide  		  will be updated at different times, detailing different hunting areas.

If you are looking for basic beginner "newbie"  		  guides, be sure to check out RPG Vault's  		  EQVault section . Since the Vault Network has a very extensive guide  		  for the various race/class combinations of Norrath, the guide that you are  		  reading will be a non-race/class specific one detailing locations around  		  Norrath that are good for any class to use.

This first installment of the guide will cover  		  levels 1 through 20.

Later installments of the guide will cover higher  		  levels, as well as the upcoming expansion The Ruins of Kunark .

...on to the Game Basics Section

For more information, including reviews  	and cheats, follow this link:

IGN's  	    Everquest Vault

Everquest  	    Coverage on IGN PC

IGN’s EverQuest Survival Guide is written  	and designed by Jeremy "Izanir" Conrad, Gnomish Wizard, Xegony

For feedback or questions, e-mail  	IGNguides at:  	.

title: Power Leveling Guide
content:
## Power Leveling Guide


What exactly is Power Leveling (PLing) in EverQuest (EQ)? by Tripodnukem, Norraths Wrecking Crew, Stromm Server

Well, simply put, its a LEGAL technique used to accellerate the speed at which one's character (toon) increases in level. Although the definition of PLing is simple, the actual act of performing PLing effectively is much more complex than many players understand. Even experienced players are often not aware HOW TO PL SOMEONE or HOW TO BE PL'd. This is often in part to experienced players of very high levels concentrating their efforts on their main toon, rather than spending time building a new toon from scratch or 'assisting' someone in building a new toon. We felt there was a need for information on this topic so we have written a guide that should help those new to the concept of PLing.

It is important to note before we get too far into details, that there will be those that disagree with the methods described in this guide. Some will say this guide is the best thing they have seen since high speed internet. Others will say its ok, but there are better methods. I'm sure there are better methods on how to PL a toon out there, but since there appears to be an absence of any kind for a strategy or guide on the internet about it, we took it upon ourselves to share our experiences on the topic of Power Leveling.

First off, it is important (not necessary but strongly suggested) that you do NOT PL solo (boxing). Unless you are a pro at boxing, don't try to PL solo. PLing is not difficult if you are an experienced boxer, but even boxers that play 4 toons at once have been known to say they prefer not to box when PLing. Find a friend or hire someone in your guild or online to perform these services for you. I would NOT pay real money to be PL'd, however if you are in need of some assistance, I guess offering another toon of a higher level some platinum or items for their time would be considered fair. You'll find that there are many players out there that will offer this, especially if they are your friends, for free. Please ensure the person you get to assist you not only has a toon that can perform the duties to help with your PLing, but also make sure they understand HOW TO PL SOMEONE. All parties must know their job and should also know the other person's job so they know what to expect and can identify problems when they arise before things get out of hand, leaving players buying soulstones (rezzes).

Any class of character can be PL'd. Period. No matter what anyone says, you can always PL your new toon. Some classes are easier to PL than others and we will go into the benefits of each class a bit later. One the other hand, NOT any class can PL. Actually it's rather funny, the easiest class to be PL'd (mage) from new is also the MOST DIFFICULT class if not IMPOSSIBLE to assist later on as a Power Leveler. And one of the hardest classes to PL from new (Druid) is actually the best class to assist later on as the Power Leveler. Now there are many difficult classes to PL from new and Druid is not necessarily the hardest but it is certainly not the easiest. The most difficult class to PL solo, and often thought IMPOSSIBLE to PL without being grouped with a similar level ranger sharing the PLing experience, is the Wizard. This class pretty much has only one way to deal damage without getting too close to the action and that are the direct damage nukes, which often draw agro. Drawing agro is almost certain death.

Ok, enough of the warning, 'cause at this stage if you are not aware of how to PL or how to be PL'd, I've lost you. So let us start from scratch. We used a high level druid (67) for this example. The level of the Power Leveler (PLer) will determine the maximum zone at which you can assist. Basically what will occur is everyone gets BUFFED up. The druid's job is to become the target for the mob(s) to hit. The druid's DS buffs will damage the mob(s) each time the mob hits the druid. Now the job of the one being Power Leveled, we will use a mage in this case, is to get their pet to hit the mob and cause damage at least once. Once the mob is damaged by the low level toon (or their pet) move onto the next mob until each mob is hit before the mobs die off from the druid's damage shield (DS). Once each mob is hit, pull back and STOP hitting. The low level toon's help in continuing to fight is pointless and the end result is often drawing agro, which mentioned earlier, means instant death. As the mobs die off from the DS, the experience will go to the toon that caused direct damage or some kind of Damage Over Time or direct damage spell. The druid will not get the credit, so long as the druid avoids hitting them with any kind of direct damage spell or weapon. One thing to watch out for is being careful not to use a root/snare spell that causes damage. If you have to root or snare the mobs, snare is often the best because they will stop in place and continue to fight; root completely immobolizes the mob, thus they will not continue to hit the druid until they drop.

Now what we did is we took a mage level 12, into a level 40 hot zone. Suicide? No. Let me explain. The druid was pulling 3 or 4 mobs at one time, any more than this and it becomes difficult to click on each mob to deal damage. The mage would then command the pet to attack the mobs one by one. (The ability to control your pet, pull him back and send him in quickly is an absolute MUST ability of the player playing the mage). In our particular group, we had a wizzy level 12 as well being boxed by the druid. But since the wizzy only has nukes that would draw agro, we just let the wizzy sit in the corner and hide. The experience rate following these simple steps allowed us to gain 10 levels for both the wizzy and the mage in 1 hour.

It is essential you do not make the mistake of having the one that is PLing you, in your group, for obvious reasons. Now I would like to point out some things you must be sure to do as the new toon being PL'd:

Try to clear out the corpses destroy lore items if needed; corpses on the ground make it difficult if not at times impossible to target your mobs communicate with your druid - don't go AFK without telling him and for how long.

DO NOT invite others into your group without the approval of the druid - no matter who is the leader of your group, it is the Druid that is the boss and without the druid, there is no power levelling group. Period.

If you are a pet class, make sure your pet is TWINKED to the teeth.

Spend the platinum to buy your pet the best pet toys platinum can buy. It is your job to land the single hit. If you cannot hit the mobs, you won't get experience.

Understand that your druid is doing this out of the goodness of their heart, even if you paid them, its most boring. If the druid wants to loot, let them. Unless they tell you to keep it all, assume everything you loot belongs to the druid and you are just holding it for them.

Bring enough bags to loot to clear the corpses over and over, destroy stuff if you must, don't run off to vendor trash it and delay the PLing experience for a few platinum.

Dont wander off and pull mobs on your own; this only causes problems and the efficiency of the pulling is cut in half over 1 single mob.

Respect the zone you are PLing in. If a group comes into the zone that is more appropriate for that zone in relation to that group's level, give up the camp. Especially if they ask politely and they wait patiently without stealling kills off your druids pulls. Power Leveling is completely legal, but out of respect for others, give up the space to appropriate levels to the zone you are in.

Avoid PLing near named mobs, you're here for the experience, not the loot or the epic drops, remember that.

Always Always Always thank the person that is power leveling you. You're rudeness may affect the next guy that needs help.

Plan bio breaks and listen to EVERYTHING the druid says. If the druid is low on mana or has to answer the phone or take a bio break, understand and remember without him, you and your entire group are hamburger.

Fighter type classes can always skill up their class skills in the arena against a high level toon in a duel. Caster classes will have to sit in their guild hall mana pools to skill up in their spell skills.

Bring your own way home. Make sure you have a way to gate out if you have to leave. Do not 'EXPECT' a ride home. Especially if it's a group being PL'd.

If you are not using a druid to PL your toon, expect to PAY for the PLer's skinspikes.

If the PLer asks you to invite a toon to your group, do it without question. More than likely its a very good friend of the PLer, or their box that cannot be PL'd solo (ie, wizzy).

In the event of death, NEVER NEVER NEVER blame the power leveller, unless you never want his or her help ever again.

Do not let general or guild chat get in the way of your job to hit each mob, loot and rest if needed. You should NEVER have to call out LOM or become low on HP's. Remember, your job is to hit a mob once, connecting with damage, and move on, then sit. However, if you are a caster-only class it may become necessary to let the druid know you are LOM if the druid is chain pulling and there is not enough break time between the pulls to allow for rest. This is another reason why it is a good idea that caster only classes group with mages or fighters so they can med.

If it becomes too dangerous, and there are too many mobs, let the druid know or don't attack all of them. It is entirely possible the druid took too long to bring back your mobs to the camp, and they started to drop before you could hit them. NO BIG DEAL, let it go. The druid is not an idiot and they will correct their strategy accordingly. Mention it nicely if the problem become persistent, to maybe bring back less mobs and why.

Being Power levelled is not something that should be done for your new toon if any of the following conditions exist:

You are poor and do not have the platinum to buy new gear once you do gain those 20 levels in a single day. Remember, you'll have a naked toon with no armor and will one day have to adventure on your own.

If the zone you want to PL in is packed full.

You have to run a group off of a camp to make room for your PLing group.

You are new to EQ, or you are new to the class you are having PL'd. Learn the class you are playing from scratch before attempting to be PL'd the second time through that class.

If you don't understand how to be PL'd or the druid (can be another class but I keep saying druid cause they are the BEST PLing class) doesn't know how to PL a new toon.

If you don't have an hour to spare to denote to being Power Leveled.

If you have less than 50,000 platinum in the bank combined on all your toons. If you have less than that, you should not PL a new toon, you cannot afford to equip your new toon to the level at which it will make it possible for your new toon to actually land a hit. Nor will you have enough platinum to equip your toon once the PLing is complete.

If you are a mage and you cannot get pet toys and there are no other tanks, postpone being PL'd. A mage's pet can be the most formidable opponent for a mob, but without being twinked, a mage's pet is worth the cost to creat the pet, nothing.

I hope this guide has allowed you to understand how power levelling is actually performed and the points that I have made will help you to become a player others will enjoy helping.

Whoever fights monsters should see to it that in the process he does not become a monster.
And when you look into an abyss, 
the abyss also looks into you.
(- Nietzsche-)
--- Tripodvi ---

content:
## New Players Guide


You might ask precisely what I mean by an “EQ-Youngin”. An EQ-Youngin is one of the more polite terms used for a player that is new to the EverQuest environment. What you are about to read is a guide for those new to EQ, although it can easily be used to perfect a quick-leveling guide when re-rolling Characters. IGN-Vault is here to assist your growth and the “Early Years” of your EverQuest experience in any and every way possible!
Section l : “Hunting Grounds and what Mobs (Monsters) to hunt!” (Levels 1-20)

Note: These “grounds” can be used by ANY class for quick and efficient leveling.

Note: Before following this guide make sure you are familiar with the “Toggle-Map-Command” (While in game click ‘M’ on your keyboard and set the “controls” at ‘100’ and ‘100’.


## Level: 1-4


Your “beginning city." Basic sewer rats in the city as well as lower-level Mobs surrounding the outskirts (Easily found).


## Level: 5-10


Zone to Level in: Black Burrow

Planes of Power Expansion: Find the teleportation-book labeled “Qeynos” in the Plane of Knowledge (Click it)

Non-Planes of Power Expansion: Find a Wizard (Teleport to West Karana) / Find a Druid (Teleport to Surefall Glade)

Mobs to hunt: Scrawny Gnolls, Gnolls, Patrolling Gnolls, Gints snakes (snake ledge)

Loot to focus on: gnoll fangs (hand them in to Captain Tillan), ANY cloth armor, a cracked staff, any gnoll body-parts that DO NOT say “NO DROP” (bones etc.)


## Level: 11-15


Zone to Level in: Crush Bone

Planes of Power Expansion: Find the teleportation-book labeled “Kelethin” in the Plane of Knowledge (Click it) -As soon as you teleport in, turn left and follow the path back to the city. Circle the “edges” of the city until you find an elevator that is slightly pushed against a mound of grass (Orc Lift). Follow the path directly in front of it STRAIGHT (Non-stop)

Non-Planes of Power Expansion: Find/contact a Wizard (Teleport to Greater Faydark Spires, then follow the path directly STRAIGHT until you reach a “Zone-line” (gouge in the wall) turn right and follow it STRAIGHT).

Mobs to hunt: Orc Legionnaires, Orc Oracles, Royal Guard, Orc Emissary

Loot to focus on: Legionnaire Pads (Fnd your way by using your map from “Greater Faydark” to “Butcher Block”, continue to use your map to locate “Kaladim”. Once you have reached “Kaladim”(The City of Dwarves) search for “Canloe Nusback” at/in the Dwarf-Warrior-Guild.))

ALTERNATE ZONE TO LEVEL IN - Black Burrow (*see top for location-directions*)

Mobs to hunt: a giant snake (“Snake Ledge”), a Gnoll Guardsmen, an Elite Gnoll Guardsmen, Gnoll Commander, Various Named Gnolls (“Elite Ledge”/”Green Room”/”Commanders Room”))

Loot to focus on: Gnoll fangs, Studded Leather Collar’s, Spiked Collar’s, Rusty Spiked Shoulder-pads))


## Level: 16-24


Zone to Level in: Paludal Caverns

Planes of Power Expansion: Find the teleportation-book labeled “Nexus” in the Plane of Knowledge (Click it) -As soon as you teleport in, turn directly around and follow the wall to your right. When you reach the zone line, continue through it...Use your map (by clicking ‘M’ on your keyboard) and find “Paludal Caverns”.

Non Planes of Power Expansion: Find/contact a Druid or a Wizard and ask them to teleport you to the “Nexus”.

Mobs to hunt: Recondite bandits, Yelloweyes (Owl-Bear), Recondite Cutpurse, Recondite Demagogue, a Recondite Pickpocket, a mature reishi sensi)

Loot to focus on: bronze brigandine armor (use, if not sell), bronze weapons))

ALTERNATE ZONE TO LEVEL IN - High Pass Hold

Location-Directions: Find/contact a Druid to teleport you to “East Karana”. As soon as you “zone in” carefully rotate your character so he or she is facing “east”. Begin running “straight” until you come upon a semi-steep mountainous-cliff area and then continue “east” past it until you come upon a steep cliff area (that gradually is descending downward). Follow the “high-path” (high-ground). It will then bring you to “High Pass Hold”.

Good luck on your guided journey, be safe and have FUN!


## Section ll : Basic Class Guides for the New/Un-familiar EverQuest player



## Warrior:


A group-oriented class, somewhat decent at dealing damage, but is more geared to taking damage for the group (“meat-shield”).

Basic Job in Groups: To keep ‘Mobs’ aggressive towards them (attacking/taunting the ‘Mob‘). *Dual-wielding Class (Using 2-Weapons)*

Note: Warriors CANNOT cast ANY spells.

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Agility, Dexterity


## Necromancer:


A solo-oriented class (*higher level group-oriented*), uses various DOTS (Damage Over Time Spells), Dis-Enchantments (Spells to weaken their enemy), skeleton pet (Specter Pet at higher-levels), semi-powerful DD spells (Direct Damage), and Life Taps (Hit Point drainage)

Basic Job in Groups: To provide mana for your group members as well as send your pet to attack the ‘Mob’, DOT the ‘Mob’ and dis-enchant the ‘Mob’.

Note: CANNOT take much damage due to low Hit Points and limited selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Intelligence, Dexterity


## Wizard


A solo-oriented class (*higher level group-oriented*), uses the MOST POWERFUL DD (Direct Damage) and AOE (Area Of Effect) spells in the game. Does the most upfront-single hit damage. Uses various “root spells” as well.

Basic Job in Groups: To “Nuke” (DD) the ‘Mob’ as much as possible.

Note: CANNOT take much damage due to low Hit Points and limited selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Intelligence, Stamina


## Magician


A solo-oriented class, uses various DD (Direct Damage) and AOE (Area Of Effect) spells and relies on Elemental Pet (Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind).

Basic Job in Groups: To deal damage using DD (Direct Damage) and AOE (Area Of Effect) spells, as well as using their pet to deal minor DD (Direct Damage) and semi-strong melee damage.

Note: CANNOT take much damage due to low Hit Points and limited selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Intelligence, Stamina


## Enchanter


A solo and group oriented class, *The Most Complex Caster-Class*, uses various Dis-Enchantments (Spells to weaken their enemy), uses various Enchanment spells (Spells to enhance the abilities of your group members), uses illusions to infiltrate enemy factions, as well as to trick and have fun on your down-time, uses weaker DD (Direct Damage) spells, uses weaker root spells, and uses weaker DOTS (Damage Over Time Spells), uses powerful “Charm” spells for soloing purposes, uses an invisible-warrior (a weaker pet then others but still useful and efficient due to quick cast time at lower levels), uses many mesmerize spells (used for crowed control).

Basic Job in Groups: To enchant your group members (feeding mana as well) and to dis-enchant 'Mobs' as well as add in DDs and DOTS from time to time.

Note: CANNOT take much damage due to low Hit Points and limited selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Intelligence, Charisma


## Druid


A solo and group-oriented class, well-rounded, using various DOTS (Damage Over Time Spells), powerful DD (Direct Damage) spells, strong-ability to root/slow your enemy, also has decent healing-spells as well, uses unique high-hitting damage-shields.

Basic Job in Groups: To “Nuke” (DD) the ‘Mob’ and assist in healing your group members.

Note: CANNOT much damage due to low Hit Points and limited selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Wisdom, Stamina


## Shaman


A solo and group-oriented class, uses semi-powerful healing spells, uses many powerful DD (Direct Damage) spells, uses many powerful DOTS (Damage Over Time Spells), has various of spells to slow and root, higher levels - use of a pet, uses many Enchantment spells as well as Dis-Enchantment spells.

Basic Job in Groups: Enchant your group members, Dis-Enchant the ‘Mob’/’Mobs’ you are hunting, use your Heals and DOTS/DD’s CAREFULLY.

Note: CANNOT take much damage due to low Hit Points and limited selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Wisdom, Stamina, Dexterity


## Cleric


A group-oriented class, uses weak DD (Direct Damage) spells, uses the MOST POWERFUL healing spells/hit point Enchantments in the game, uses many stuns.

Basic Job in Groups: Distribute heals and “buffs” (Enchantments/Enhancements) throughout the group.

Note: CANNOT take a lot of damage due to low Hit Points.

Key Attributes: Wisdom, Stamina


## Paladin


A solo and group-oriented class, uses basic Cleric spells (heals, stuns, buffs) and has a unique “Paladin-only” spell known as “Lay on Hands” (Instant Heal spell). More geared towards a warrior, wide-selection of armor types.

Basic Job in Groups: To assist the warrior in damage absorbed/deal damage, and crowed control (using stuns).

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Wisdom


## Shadow Knight


A solo and group-oriented class, uses basic Necromancer spells (DOTS, Life Taps, skeleton pet (weak), Dis-Enchantments) and has a unique “Shadow Knight-only” spell known as “Death Touch” (Instant Direct Damage spell). More geared towards a warrior, wide-selection of armor types.

Basic Job in Groups: To assist the warrior in damage absorbed/deal damage, and to weaken the opposing ‘Mob’ with unholy Dis-Enchantments.

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Intelligence, Dexterity


## Beast Lord


A solo-oriented class, uses basic Shaman spells (minor DOTS, Dis-Enchantments, Slows, Minor Heals) and has a unique series of “Beast Lord-only” spells such as creating a wildlife pet to fight for you in battle (Trolls-Alligators|Ogres-Bears|Barbarians-Wolves|Iksars-Scaled Wolves|Vah Shirs-Tigers). You are also given many spells to enhance your pet such as Damage-Enhancing Enchantments, and Pet heals.

Basic Job in Groups: To “dish out” as much damage as possible and to Dis-Enchant the ‘Mob’/’Mobs’. *Dual-wielding Class (Using 2-Weapons)*

NOTE: Limited Selection of High-AC Armor

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Wisdom, Dexterity


## Ranger:


A solo and group-oriented class, uses basic Druid spells (minor heals, damage shields, minor DD’s (Direct Damage Spells), and mediocre roots and snares. Powerful with Bows (Can perform high-damage critical hits with them) and has a unique “Ranger-only” self-Enchantment spell that Quickens attack speed.

Basic Job in Groups: To “dish out” as much damage as possible and to assist in snaring. *Dual-wielding Class (Using 2-Weapons)*

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Wisdom, Dexterity


## Rogue


A group-oriented class, deals an insane amount of upfront damage with ‘backstab’-skill. Has many neat tricks (Hide, Sneak, Pickpocket). Uses various poisons to deal even MORE damage.

Basic Job in Groups: To “dish out” as much damage as possible using basic melee and backstabs. *Dual-wielding Class (Using 2-Weapons)*

NOTE: Limited Selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Strength, Dexterity, Stamina, Agility


## Monk:


A group-oriented class, deals high damage due to various Martial-Art abilities (Different “moves”) and has High AC due to carrying less weight. Has a unique self-heal ability (‘Mend’). Can ‘feign-death’ so as to escape trouble at later levels.

Basic Job in Groups: To “dish out” as much damage as possible using their unique “martial-art abilities”, and to also pull ’Mobs’ using their “feign-death’ ability (control pulling). *Dual-wielding Class (Using 2-Weapons)*

NOTE: Limited Selection of High-AC Armor.

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Agility, Dexterity


## Bard


A solo and group-oriented class, has the unique ability to twist-songs, uses “songs”(spells) that are based on “a-little of everything”, the bard can heal, regenerate mana, DD (Direct Damage), AOE (Area Of Effect), Slow, Snare, Charm, DOT (Damage Over Time), Enchant, Dis-Enchant, and Mesmerize. The bard is the most well-rounded class and probably one of the most difficult classes to play. The “Bard” class is known for being the BEST DUELING-CLASS in the game. .

Basic Job in Groups: To assist in minor damage, but to continuously twist your songs (whichever group asks for) and on downtime twist the mana and health songs.

*Dual-wielding Class (Using 2-Weapons)*

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Charisma, Dexterity


## Berserker


A group-oriented class, has unique stun/snare abilities, uses 2-handed slash ONLY, has the ability to “Frenzy” (Triple swing-’Three’ hits).

Basic Job in Groups: To “dish out” as much damage as possible using “Frenzy” and basic melee, and also to snare and slow "mobs.".

Key Attributes: Strength, Stamina, Dexterity

I wish you luck on whichever path you choose to follow, my friend! May the ‘magic’ of EverQuest bring you fortune on your journey.

content:
## Ranger 101


07-11-2004 - First, the reason for this guide. After having read many other guides I find all of them lacking in some way for the truly new Everquest player. This guide is an effort to give the new Everquest player what he needs to have fun for the first month or so of gameplay. After that you will have a better idea of what you would like to do yourself and you won't need someone else telling you what to do. Because I believe the Ranger class is the easiest class for the new Everquest player, this is also a good beginning Ranger Guide.

The first thing you will do is choose your Race, Class and God. You want to be a Half-elf Ranger worshiping Karana. Why? Three reasons: First, as a Half-elf you get infravision. It is annoying to play a human at night. Either you need a light source or you can't see at night, especially in the dark tunnels. With infravision you will hardly notice the difference between day and night. Second, as a Ranger you get tracking. This is the best skill in the game for a new player. With one key press you get a list of every creature within range of you and how tough they are. And finally, by worshiping Karana, the rain god, you get to start in Surefall Glade, the best place for a new player to start. It is small, quiet and safe. You don't need a map to find your way around, you will be one of the only players in the Glade, so your message window will not be filled with "spam" and you can always just sit down beside your guild master to rest in perfect safety. After choosing your race and class you will have 20 "extra" points to put into your starting attributes. I suggest you put 10 points into wisdom to bring your total to 75 (the minimum needed to succeed with your spells) and 10 points into dexterity to bring your total to 95 (needed to excel at your second best ability, archery). For more about rangers and tracking see note 1 at the end of this article.

Now once you enter the game you will start in the ranger's guild. Look at your inventory (hit the "I" key). Notice you have a sword and a note. Left click on the sword to select it and put it into your "hand" space. To read the note right click on it. Now go outside (left click on the door to open it) to the archery practice field (over the little bridge and around to the right) to find your guild master. Give him the note (left click on the note, then click the note on him). He will give you a tunic (put it on) and tell you who your trainer is. Go to your trainer (he is at the fire between the ranger's guild and the archery field). Right click on him and select the skills you want to be trained in. Train at least one point in 1H slash and one point in Tracking. Choose other skills that look interesting (like fishing) or just put the last three into 1H slash. Don't worry, you will get 5 more "points" every level so if you miss something now you will get a chance to train for it later. Tracking is your most important skill but you only need one point to get it (and all of your other skills) started. All of your skills will increase as you use them (and you will use tracking a lot).

Before I go any further there is one thing you need to do. The various Everquest commands have "short cut" keys that they have been mapped to. One of the most important that you will use all of the time is the auto attack key. This key is defaulted as the "A" key. You should remap it to another key that you will not be using to type any messages (like the "=" key). You can do this by selecting the options button from the window selection. Just go through the list of commands and select the auto attack command, then hit the new key you want to use for it.


## Level 1-2


Now follow the path leading away from the ranger's guild to the right around the cliff and into the tunnel. This is where you will like having a half-elf instead of a human. At night this tunnel gets so dark you cannot see a thing, if you are a human. As a Half-elf you will hardly notice any difference. About 80% of the way through the tunnel you will "zone" to Qeynos Hills. Your screen will freeze. Don't panic, your computer is just loading all of the info for the new area. When it finishes just keep going until you are at the other end of the tunnel. Step just outside the exit and have a look around.

Qeynos Hills is your happy hunting ground for at least your first 5 levels. The two guards at the entrance are your friends. If you get into trouble just run back to the tunnel entrance and they will take care of any monsters that are chasing you. To find the location of the tunnel entrance, just type /loc. Remember this number; write it down. Now set up tracking as one of your hot keys (in the window with the four tabs, select the skills tab, click on a number and select tracking) and click on it. Notice the list of things that came up on the tracking screen. At the bottom of the screen select the "range" option for the sort order. Each creature within your tracking range will show up on this screen color coded by how tough they are for you and sorted in the order of distance from you. Red are the toughest (don't mess with these), then yellow (very risky), white (an even fight, these are the ones you will be fighting most of the time). Because you are only first level nothing will show up blue (easier, you should win) or green (a cake walk) yet. The best creatures to attack now are Snakes and Skeletons. There are different versions of each of these creatures so be sure you are only tracking the white ones. Click on one of them and then click on the track button and you will start getting messages telling you which direction your victim is in. Turn (hit the right or left arrow keys) until your messages say your victim is straight ahead, then start running (hit the up arrow key) until you see it.

Now right click on the thing you see to be sure it is the same thing you are tracking. Then left click on it to target it, hit your auto attack key, then move until you are right next to your victim. If you are attacking snakes (or other low creatures) you should hit the page down (3 on the number pad) key to "look down" at your victim so you can see him. Once the music starts and you see the attack messages, the fight is on. Watch your health bar. As soon as it gets down to 60% (two of the 5 "bubbles") look at your victim's health. If it is down further than yours you are doing fine, just sit there and enjoy the battle. If it has not moved very much (still shows 80-100%, only down one "bubble", then it is time to run. If you used "Page Down", hit the 5 key on the number pad to look straight ahead. Turn around until you can see the cliff face, the tunnel entrance and your two friendly guards. Run for the tunnel entrance. Keep running until you are just inside the entrance. Then turn around. If you are lucky you will see your two friends kill your victim for you.

If you win the fight, you get to loot the body. Right click on the corpse, then right click on the items. The best ones are the snake jaws and poison sacks, and the skeleton tibias. Try to concentrate on only two types of victims because you can only carry 6 different kinds of loot at this time. Now click on done and then go back to the tunnel entrance.

Now weather you won or lost your battle, rest at the tunnel entrance until your health is 100% and then repeat the above hunting directions. Never go too far from the tunnel entrance and the guards. Always start by using your track ability to find the snakes and skeletons you want to kill. Keep this up until you cannot carry anything else or until you have reached level three, or until you have had enough for one night. When you are done go back through the tunnel into Surefall Glade and camp for the night. In order to leave the game, click on the sit button, then on the camp button. After 30 seconds you will leave the game. When you restart Everquest and reenter the game you will appear in this exact location to start your next game play session.

When you need to sell your loot, go into the ranger's guild and enter the room to the right. Behind the counter there are three merchants. Right click on the middle one and sell your loot by clicking the item and then on the sell button. Notice that there is a number next to most of the items you looted. These are "stackable" items. You can have up to 20 of one item type per "box" in your inventory if they are stackable. If they are not stackable then each item will take up one box. That is why you wanted to kill only snakes and skeletons and take only the poison sacks, jawbones and tibias. You should get about 2gp for each one of these items. When you are done you will want to buy at least two backpacks, but no more than 4, so you can carry more than 6 different things the next time you go hunting.


## Level 3-4


Once you reach level three you are ready to become an archer. Start by going back to your trainer and put one point into archery and one point into fletching. Go to the ranger's guild merchant and buy a quiver. Now go over to the archery range and see Jarse Kedison. Right click on him and buy a fletching kit, for about 1pp. Then buy three bundles (20 items per bundle) of each of the four parts of an arrow: points, shafts, fletchings, and nocks. Buy the cheapest one of each type: field, wood, round and large. They should cost about 6 cp each. Now find a nice quiet spot and sit down. You are going to practice making arrows. Open (right click) on your fletching kit, your backpack and your quiver. Put one bundle (20 items) of each arrow part into the top four slots of your backpack (while holding down the shift key, click on one of your arrow parts, then put them into one box of your "open" backpack). Now while holding down the Ctrl key, click on one arrow part and move it into your fletching kit. Repeat for the other three parts. Be sure you have one (and only one) of each arrow part in the fletching kit. Now hit combine. If you are lucky your pointer just turned into 5 arrows. If not don't worry, it will eventually. If it worked, put your new arrows into your ammo slot and repeat the process. Yes you are going to do this at least 60 times. Once your ammo slot is full (has 20 arrows in it) start putting your arrows into your quiver. Also notice that every once in a while you will get a message that your fletching skill has gone up. You want to keep doing this until your skill gets to 16. If you need to buy another set of arrow parts do so and keep making arrows until your fletching skill equals 16. Once it reaches 16 however, stop making arrows. It is time to make a bow.

Now go into the ranger's guild and see Tonsia and buy a hickory staff and a piece of hemp string. Put these into your fletching kit, hit combine and you should have a brand new bow. If not try again. Put the bow into the bow box of your inventory. Once you have a quiver full of arrows and a new bow it is time to go hunting. One last note on arrow and bow making. If you should run out of money before completing the process (fletching skill 16 and a completed bow) return to Qeynos Hills and kill a few more snakes and skeletons. However, if all you killed and collected was the items I mentioned above you should not need to. For more about fletching, see note 2 at the end of this article

Before you leave Surefall Glade go back to your trainer and put one point into foraging. Until now you have been eating (bread) and drinking (water) automatically. You start the game with 20 "units" of each item and you use about one item of each per game day. Eventually you will run out of them and start to get hungry and thirsty. One of the ways you can cure this is to forage for food and water. Put forage on a hot key like you did tracking and every time you see that you can, hit it. Your forage skill will increase very slowly (compared with your other skills, like fletching) and you won't have much success for a while, but eventually you will be able to feed yourself for free. If you have any "extra" training points you may want to put some of them into foraging to help it along.

Go back out into Qeynos Hills, and track as before, but now you can track anything that shows blue or white. Don't bother with anything that shows green because they are so easy that you will get little if any experience for killing them. And do not hunt wolves and bears; they are your friends. I would also stay away from Gnoll pups. You can handle them but if you start killing them now they will start attacking you without warning. You don't need someone beating on your back when you are tying to kill that skeleton. When you have tracked your victim within sight, instead of walking up to it, you are now going to shoot it with your new bow and arrows. Click on the range attack button (on your attack screen) and you will shoot an arrow at your victim. Now for the fun part. As soon as you shoot, hit the down arrow key and start backing up. When your range attack button comes back up, hit it again. You should be able to get off 2-3 shots before your victim closes the range and starts to attack you. Now hit your auto attack key and enjoy the fact that you start the fight with your victim already wounded. If your victim tries to run away before you have a chance to kill him: turn off auto attack (hit your auto attack key again), follow him at a safe distance and shoot him with your bow to finish him off. By using both your bow and sword in every fight you should advance both skills nicely.

Continue to hunt at the "north end" of Qeynos Hills, killing anything that shows white or blue until you get to level 5. You can go a little further from the guards, just stay near the road so you don't get lost. Do not go over the hill to the "east side" of Qeynos hills. There lies death at the hands of some very big skeletons and Gnolls. Stay within sight of the cliff face. If you do get lost, first try tracking the guards. If they show on your list, just track back to them. If they are too far away to track, then use the /loc command and get back to the guards that way. You did write down the location of the guards didn't you?

If you run out of arrows then go back to Jarse Kedison in Surefall Glade and buy a new set of arrow parts, but this time use the medium nocks. Combine them as before and keep making this type of arrow until your fletching skill gets to 36. Continue to sell you victim's parts to the merchant in the ranger's guild each time you come back to Surefall Glade. Note how much the different parts sell for and concentrate on killing and looting the best things (stackable items that sell for at least 2gp each).


## Level 5-6


Now once you get to level 5 it is time for your quest to begin. Go to Errin Pinewhisper in the ranger's guild. Left click on him and type /hail. He will say something to you with a couple of words in brackets []. Answer him using these key words and he will tell you about the pine scout armor quest. Ask about each armor item and write down the ingredients. Take the box he gives you and put the armor templates he gives you into it for now. Now go to your trainer and train one point in kick. To use it set up a hot key for it similar to what you did for tracking and foraging except this time put it under the attack tab. Whenever you are in melee with a creature click on kick. You will get an extra attack every 2-3 swings. Every little bit helps. Finally make up a fresh batch of arrows as before but this time using parabolic fletchings, then head back out to Qeynos Hills.

Now that you are level 5 you can hunt anywhere along the road in Qeynos hills. You are going to travel to the middle of Qeynos hills to the little house. Just follow the road south from the tunnel until you can see the house. Notice that there are two guards here as well. Now do a /loc and write done the numbers. This will be your home for a while. Now get out that ingredient list and look for the large/giant field rats and the large/giant whiskered bats. These are your new victims. Start hunting them. Remember only hunt them if they show white or blue. The one exception is a rat or bat that you need that shows yellow IF you find him close to the house/road and your weapon skills are 30+ and you are feeling lucky. If you can get 3 good bowshots and a couple more good hits with your sword and kick before your victim starts pounding on you, you might win vs. a yellow creature. But if your victim is not almost dead when you get down to 50%, health run for the house and the guards. These are big creatures and it will take more than one hit for the guards to finish them off.

By the way if you die at anytime before you reach level 10 don't worry. You will be "resurrected" with all of your stuff at the north end of Qeynos Hills. That is one of the good things about being a new player. There is no penalty for dieing until you reach level 10. But you want to get into the habit of not dieing now because it can be a real pain later.

Now whenever you get all of your rat and bat items or you reach level 6 or you get tired of Qeynos Hills you will need to get those 17 silk threads. You will make them from 34 spiderling silks. The easiest place I have found to get spiderling silk is Toxxulia Forest. It is a little trip but you are up to it. Keep heading south (away from Surefall Glade) along the Qeynos Hills road until you "zone" into North Qeynos. Keep following the road into the city. Now Qeynos can be very confusing but we are only interested in going to the docks for now. Once you enter the city "keep your right hand on the wall". What I mean by that is if you can turn right, do so. Keep following the path. If the path turns keep following it but if you can go left/straight/right, go right. Eventually you will come to a dock. Now check what time it is: type /time. You want to be on the dock at 8am. I don't know what other times the ship comes (if at all) but I have always caught it at 8am (game time). When the ship arrives just walk out along the dock and onto the ship. After a few minutes the ship will leave and you will see the city of Qeynos fade into the distance. After another few minutes you will "zone" into Erudin Crossing, and then into Erudin. When the floating dock comes out to meet the ship in Erudin get onto it. Wait for it to return to the dock. Then walk off of the dock and onto the wood pier. Now walk around and explore. You will find a "transporter" platform that will take you to Erudin proper. You will see a sign that says welcome to Erudin. Step off of the platform and turn right. Follow the path around to the right again keeping your right hand on the wall just like before until you enter a tunnel and "zone" into Toxxulia Forest.

Do a /loc. Write down the number. Also note that the "guards" here are called sentinels. Use the same methods as before to get back to your safe spot if you get lost (and you will). Now Toxxulia Forest is not Qeynos Hills. It is a dark and confusing forest. This is where your tracking skill will really shine. Start tracking widow hatchlings and spiderlings. Notice that they both show green or blue. This means that they will be very easy to kill. Notice also that almost everything else shows green or blue. This means that you have little to fear from anything in the forest. This is good because almost everything in here hates you. They will attack you if you get too close to them so don't walk up next to anything other than the 'lings that you are after. The hatchlings and spiderlings will drop between 0 and 6 spiderling silks each. So it should not take you very long to collect your 34 silks. If you are attacked by a "stranger" right click on it. If it shows green or blue and you feel like it kill it. If not run back to the tunnel entrance. You may have to "zone" back to Erudin to avoid your attacker. The sentinels are not as nice about killing your attackers as the guards in Qeynos Hills were. After all you are the stranger here. One more thing, if a poacher attacks you, you will want to kill him and save his head. You can return it to Gillarian Naelev in Surefall Glade for some experience and other benefits.

Now that you have your spiderling silk it is time to head back to Qeynos hills. Go back through the tunnel into Erudin and again keep your right hand on the wall. You will find a teleport platform in the "north east" corner of Erudin that will take you back to the dock. Again check the time and wait on the floating dock until the boat shows up. Enjoy the ride back to Qeynos. To get back to Qeynos hills keep you left hand on the wall this time and you will find the city exit and the road to Qeynos Hills. On your way you will want to stop at Fhara's Leather and Thread and buy a small sewing kit from Fhara Sernhart. As soon as you exit the dock you will turn left. The first small building you come to is Fhara's. Once you get back to Qeynos hills hunt there near the house until you are level 7, then head back home to Surefall Glade. For more information about Qeynos and Erudin see note 3 at the end of this article.


## Level 7-8


Now it is time to complete the quest. First go to your trainer and train one point in tailoring. Now make the silk thread by putting two spiderling silks into the small sewing kit (in two separate boxes, don't stack them) and combining them (just like you made all those arrows). Repeat the process until you have 17 threads. Now take all of your quest items and organize them in a bag or two so you are ready to make each piece of armor as soon as you get the ruined gnoll chain piece you need to complete each one. Also don't forget to make a new batch of arrows. This time use med nocks and parabolic fletchings. This will give you longer ranged arrows so you can start hitting your victims even further away. If you collected some poacher heads don't forget to give them to Gillarian Naelev in the ranger's guild. For more about quests see note 4 at the end of this article.

If you have not collected all of the items you need for your armor don't give up. After having killed so many rats and bats you will have noticed that some of the items are NO DROP. This means that the person who looted that item is the only one that can use it. You cannot sell it, traded it, or even drop it. The only way to get rid of it is to destroy it. The NO DROP items that you need are the only ones that you must get for yourself. The rest you can buy from the merchants or even from other players. So if you are missing something look for it at the merchants in the house in Qeynos Hills and the ranger's guild in Surefall Glade.

Now go back out into Qeynos Hills and find a group. You will need help with the gnolls. You want the big ones because they are the ones with the armor. The little pups will not have any. Do a /who and see who else is around. Look for warriors, paladins, clerics, druids and rangers level 5-10. Ideally you want 2 warriors, a paladin, a cleric, and a druid (you are the ranger), but you will have to take what you can get. You can also see who is in Surefall Glade and North/South Qeynos by typing /who all 5 10. You will get a list of everyone in the game who is level 5-10 and where they are. Then use /tell [their name] to ask them if they would like to help you kill gnolls in blackburrow. Tell them that they can have any treasure the gnolls have, but you get the ruined gnoll chain armor parts. Have everyone meet you at the house in the middle of Qeynos Hills. To invite the others to join you left click on them then click the invite button on your group window.

To get to Blackburrow from the house, head north east to loc 3200,-1000. Go into the cave entrance in the cliff face. Blackburrow is an "open" three level dungeon. The first level is a clearing with a "hole" in the center. Gnolls will "spawn" (appear out of thin air) all around the clearing. Most of the higher level ones are on level two and three but for now start with the ones on level one. Tell your group to stay near you, near the cave entrance, with the warriors in the front with you and the clerics and druids behind you.. Target one of the "Gnolls" on the far side of the clearing with your bow and start shooting. He will run around the hole, gathering one or two of his friends and run toward you. Keep shooting until they come to you. Have the warriors take them on in hand-to-hand and have the clerics and druids heal the warriors. If needed you can step in with your sword and help finish off the Gnolls. If any of the Gnolls starts to run away have a druid cast snare on it and you arrow it to death. If things get too tough, (someone falls below 40% health) run for exit (that is why you stayed near the cave entrance). Go into the tunnel and "zone" back to Qeynos Hills, the Gnolls will not follow you into the next zone. Stay in the tunnel until you have a chance to heal up then go back into Blackburrow. Be very alert when first entering Blackburrow, especially if you see another group of players sitting around in the tunnel. There may be many Gnolls at the entrance that have been "trained" to the exit by the last group that got into trouble. And if you see the message "train" while in Blackburrow, be on the alert. It means that someone is leading a group of Gnolls toward the exit from the levels below. This is what you want if there are not too many of them and there are enough of you. Watch for them to appear across the clearing from you, target one of them and start shooting. Enter the fight the same way as before but watch you health closely. With a lot of Gnoll guards, commanders and shamans you can get hurt very quickly. Again if things get rough just run back into the tunnel and zone.

As soon as you kill a gnoll (or group of gnolls) and the area is quiet, loot the gnolls and take any ruined chain armor they have. Let the others have the rest. The next time you have to zone back to Qeynos Hills to rest, take the ruined armor piece and the other ingredients and put them in the quest box and combine them to make your new piece of armor. Soon you will look very cool in your complete set of pine scout armor.


## Level 9 and beyond


At this point you are no longer a newbie. You should have finished your quest (and have the armor to prove it), have excelled in fighting (archery), your unique skill (tracking) and a useful trade skill (fletching). Now you get to start using magic. Go back to your trainer in Surefall Glade and train one point each in Abjuration, Alteration, Divination, and Evocation (four of the five spell types, you won't need the last one Conjuration) and Channeling (the "core" skill for magic users). Go to the merchants in the ranger's guild and buy the following set of level 9 ranger spells: Endure Fire, Flame Lick, Glimpse, Minor Healing, Skin Like Wood and Snare. Write them into your spell book and memorize them. Go outside and start practicing them. Throw the helpful ones (Endure Fire, Glimpse, Minor Healing and Skin Like Wood) on yourself and any other new rangers (level 1-5) running around the North end of Qeynos hills. Remember when you were a new ranger and how much you liked it when someone healed you or made your skin like wood? Now you can return the favor. Practice using Snare and Flame Lick on the lower level (green and blue) creatures. Slow them down with Snare then cast Flame Lick, then run away from them. Or Snare a creature and then shoot it while running backwards.

What you do from here is up to you. You can go back to Blackburrow and hunt some more Gnolls, this time trying the second and third levels of the "dungeon". You can hunt lions and spiders in West Karana where you can use all of your ranger skills to their fullest. You can explore Qeynos. Talk to the merchants and NPCs and see what kind of quests they would like you to do. You can take up another trade skill like baking or brewing where you can use all those things you have been foraging. You can talk to the rangers and druids in Surefall Glade. Many of them have other quests that you can perform now, including the "follow on" quest from Errin Pinewhisper, where you can get the Pine Scout Sword to match your armor. You are also now experienced enough to start on the first of the ranger only quests, the trueshot longbow. It will take you to another continent before you are finished but this is a great way to see the world with a purpose. See note 5 below for more about the trueshoot longbow quest.

Or you can start a brand new character. Now that you have seen a little of the Everquest world through the eyes of an easy to play character you might want the challenge of a pure magic user, or the intrigue of a rogue or the raw killing power a pure warrior. It is up to you. Have fun and if you every need any help look for me on The Seventh Hammer.

Danian Half-Elf Ranger of Karana The Seventh Hammer


## Notes


1. THE reason for playing a ranger is the tracking skill. Only three classes get this skill and no one else gets it at level one (druids get it at level 20 and bards at level 35). This is the most useful skill for the new player because it does so much with only one key press. Frankly I don't see how any other class ever finds anything they want without tracking. One of the things you may want to do is offer to help other players track down the creatures and NPCs they are looking for. You can group with a warrior, tell him to follow you, lead him to within bow range of the thing they are hunting, fire off one of your arrows to draw it to you, then let them bash it to death. You get a share of the experience for using your unique skill without the risk of having to fight hand-to-hand.

2. For everything you ever wanted to know about fletching see the web site: https://members.bellatlantic.net/%7Eewj/fletchguide/ . This is absolutely the best guide to fletching. As a ranger you should become at least a master fletcher (fletching skill = 100), if for no other reason than to make yourself a decent bow and keep yourself stocked with arrows (much better and cheaper than anything you can get from a merchant).

3. If you have any trouble finding your way around Qeynos or Erudin, or you just want to explore them (or anywhere else for that mater) without getting lost, see the web site: https://www.eqatlas.com/ . This site has the best set of maps of Everquest I have found.

4. The reason I chose the Pine Scout Armor quest is because there is a similar armor quest for just about every race/class/god combination in Everquest. All of these quests can be completed by "newbie" characters, level 5-9. This will give the new character something to do during their formation years and they will have a set of magical armor that is better than anything they can typically afford at this point (level 9) when they are done. Also each of these armor quests has a "follow on" weapon quest resulting in a good class specific magic weapon. Notice that all of these items are no drop (you cannot give or sell them to another NPC or PC, they belong to you and you alone), Lore (you can have only one of each of them, so don't loose it) and Magic (effective vs "magic only" creatures). Not a bad start for a level 9 character.

5. The Trueshoot Longbow is an involved quest and the first "major" quest for a ranger. If you are careful you can accomplish this quest while still only level 9. For a "walkthrough" of this quest see the web site: https://www.eqrangers.com/ . One of the hardest parts of this quest will simply be getting to Freeport. You will have to run all the way across the continent from Qeynos to Freeport. It is a long way, crossing no less than 7 'zones' including two very dangerous ones. Once you are in Freeport the rest will be easy by comparison. The last part of the quest is the actual making of the bow. The higher your fletching skill the better chance you will have to make the bow but plan on many failures. I would suggest you have a fletching skill of at least 150 and enough 'parts' for at least 20 tries before you get to Kelethin. You don't want to go all the way back to Freeport and start the quest all over again just because you only had enough parts for one try. Just like with the other bows and arrows you made there is a chance that you will 'lack the skill to fashion the components into something useful'.

## Beastlord 101



## Introduction


Beastlord is the second newest class to Everquest. Primarily a pet class, it focuses on DPS (damage per second), although the Beastlord is able to perform many other roles. Beastlord is one of the three classes that can increase mana regeneration. Bard and Enchanter are the other two. It’s safe to refer to a Beastlord as the “jack of all trades” class.

Being a hybrid between Shaman and Monk, your equipment selection is rather small. For weapons you can take your pick of 1 handed blunt, 2 handed blunt, piercing and hand to hand. Leather armor is your only choice for protective gear.

At level 9 you will be able to cast your first spell. That is also when your pet, the bread and butter of this class, comes into the picture.


## Creation


Your first choice when creating a beastlord will be your race. This is strictly preference. There are a few advantages and disadvantages to each. Another thing that might effect your final decision is that your pet is dependant on your race. Example: Vah Shir, the cat race, gets a tiger as pet.


## Barbarian


Barbarian is a good aligned race. A wolf would be your pet.

Strong points:

Third best melee stats of all races.

Strong wisdom.

Weak points:

No night vision.


## Iksar


Iksar is an evil aligned race. A scaled wolf would be your pet.

Strong points:

Innate health regeneration, swimming, foraging and armor.

Agility.

Infra-vision


## Ogre


Ogre is not an evil race although they are generally disliked. A bear would be your pet.

Strong points:

Best melee stats of all races.

Can’t be stunned from the front.

Some night vision.

Weak points:

Low wisdom.


## Troll


Troll is an evil aligned race. A bear would be your pet.

Strong points:

Second best melee stats of all races.

Innate health regeneration.

Some night vision


## Vah Shir


Vah Shir is a neutral race. A tiger would be your pet.

Strong points:

Well balanced stats.

Innate safe-fall.

Weak points:

Innate hunger (will eat food faster than all other races).

Once you have selected your race, the next choice will be where to put your bonus stat points. As a Beastlord you will receive 20 points do with which to do as you please. It is recommended to put these points in wisdom. Wisdom affects your mana pool which drains as you cast spells. It is also one of the harder stats to find equipment that raises it.

Your next choice is religion. Unless you are picking a religion for role-playing reasons, it would be best to stay Agnostic. Religion can play a part in your faction, which can cause others to not like you.


## Alternate Advancement


This section is dedicated to answering a few of your questions regarding AA abilities once you start getting within reach of the end game.


## General Abilities


Since you have to pick 6 of these to get to the next they need to be addressed.

Run 3 will prove invaluable. When entering an area where the casting of movement speed increasing spells is not permitted, you will thank this guide for advising you to take this ability.

Innate Regeneration. You can never really have enough regeneration going -- the more the better. Considering your other choices, this may be the best.

Innate Metabolism. Some choose to take this over Innate Regeneration. If you are Vah Shir it would be advisable. This ability decreases the amount of food you eat. Stat food users will learn to love this ability also.

The rest of the abilities are merely ok. It is recommended to go on with other abilities before coming back to these. There shouldn’t be any rush to get them.


## Melee/Priest Archetypes Abilities


This is when the AA choices really start to open up. There are a few goodies here that will be explained.

Combat Agility is great for any Beastlord who plans to take hits. This skill gives you a greater chance not to get hit at all.

Combat Fury will give you the ability to score critical hits. If you are looking for ways to increase your damage per second, this would be an ideal choice.

Combat Stability works somewhat like Combat Agility. The difference is that Stability actually kicks in when you are hit, decreasing the amount of damage you take. Combat Agility and Stability go hand in hand.

Finishing Blow is another skill that you may want to come back to later in life. The catch here is that the majority of the mobs you will be fighting at this level are going to be out of the level range of this ability.

Natural Durability increases your hit points with each train. You really can’t go wrong here. No matter how you spend your time in game, you will benefit from having more hit points.

Natural Healing is another health regeneration increaser. Come back for it, eventually.

Healing Adept increases the amount of health that you heal per cast. Good for a soloing beast, as it gives more healing for less mana.

Healing Gift gives you the ability to score the occasional “Exceptional Heal," which works just like a critical. Occasional, however, being the keyword.


## Beastlord Abilities


It only gets better from this point on.

Ambidexterity is quite the expensive choice, but it will indeed increase your damage per second. If that is what you’re looking for, this is the ticket.

Frenzy of Spirit will turn you into a monster until it runs out. This works like your discipline Beastial Fury, except that it's much more effective and only has a 15 minute recharge timer. If you’re looking for damage, pick it up.

Hobble of Spirits is a great ability. You may perhaps want to hold off on getting it though. The ability to snare can be great, but there are better choices.

Mend Companion is another great choice to look into. With Mend and Hastened Mending, chosen from Planar Abilities, you will be able to nearly complete heal your pet every 9 minutes.

Paragon of Spirit should be had as soon as possible. It gives you the ability to cast a spell, that doesn’t take mana, which will regenerate your group's mana and health over 6 ticks. This alone can often kill the need for downtime.

Pet Discipline is like sending your warder to obedience school. You order him to hold and he will sit and watch you die before he attacks without the command. Very useful and should be acquired as soon as possible.

Physical Enhancement is like training Natural Durability, Combat Agility and Combat Stability all at once. If you are going that route with your Beastlord, don’t forget to pick this up.


## Planar Advancement


Most of these have a pre-requirement. For example, Lightning Reflexes requires that you have completed Combat Agility.

Innate Defense will further decrease the amount of damage you take if hit by a melee attack.

Lightning Reflexes will further decrease the amount that you are actually hit.

Beastial Frenzy will give you the ability to double attack. Beastlords do not get this by default like some of the other classes. For each train it increases your damage per second even more. If this is the route you are taking, you probably should start here.

Suspended Minion gives you the ability to put your pet in your pocket. You can travel across an area and take him out once you get there. After your second train, suspending him keeps his buffs intact.

Fury of Ages increases your chance to score a critical hit. If you have Combat Fury, this will only make it better.


## Gates of Discord Abilities


Many of these are just for fun.

Swift Journey will increase your run speed even farther after getting run speed 3.

Convalescence will increase your health and mana regeneration even more. You need Mind and Body Rejuvenation to train this.

Weapon Affinity will increase the amount your weapons “proc”. For a Beastlord this is something like a double edged sword. A Proc can generate aggro -- something you may not want.

Bestial Alignment will turn you into a warder and lasts for 30 seconds. During this time you are a little more resistant and will perform like your warder. The more trains you take, the more damage.

Feral swipe is another fun ability. It just adds to your array of attacks. It has a one minute timer, and if you manage to critical with a 2 handed blunt weapon while using this, it will be a beautiful thing.

Warder Fury will increase your pet’s damage per second by giving him the ability to score critical hits.

Warders Alacrity will give your pet the ability to flurry. Flurry gives you an extra attack for that round of combat.

Mastery of the Past is worth at least one train, unless you managed to keep up your casting skills during that long road to 65. Training eliminates the chance to fizzle up to the intended spell level.

Sinister strikes ability is another damage per second increaser. By now you’ve noticed that you hit a lot weaker with your off hand. This will give it a little more power.

A few notes on Alternate Advancement...

Taking your most common role into consideration you will probably want to go with the more health and damage avoidance oriented approach when starting out. Paragon, MGB and Pet hold are often requirements to get into a raiding guild and with good reason. Paragon and MGB can be used together. If the coordination is there, you can have constant mana regeneration through the hard part of an encounter. You can’t beat that with a stick. Pet hold is just a no compromise. Stray pets can often cause an entire raid to fail.


## General Tips


Your hand to hand skill will rise beyond any of your other attack skills, although it is best to keep them all as high as you can. Make sure that hand to hand stays at the max for your level.

Your primary stats are going to be strength, stamina and wisdom. These affect your damage, health and mana respectively. When considering upgrades, keep this in mind.


## Grouping Tips


This may be hard to remember at times but you must always keep your pet’s taunt off. Each time you summon a pet, you will have to turn this back off. Your pet can generate a lot of aggro. The monster will direct that aggro towards you, not the pet. The healer and tank of the group probably won’t appreciate this.

Spells such as slow and weaken can really draw aggro. If possible, wait a few seconds to join the fight after casting one of these on the mob. If resisted, make sure you’re well out of range before you try again.

At 44 you will be able to learn the spell Spiritual Light. This spell gives you and your group increased mana and health regeneration. The effects are somewhat minimal but every little bit counts. Later in your life you will have access to a few other spells like this.

Know your role. When joining an already established group don’t be afraid to ask what needs to be done. Not knowing you’re the slower could cause disaster.

Watch for pet push. Pet placement is a critical aspect that you will have to learn at some point. A pet has the ability to push the mob. It’s usually best to angle your pet toward the tank a few steps out. That way you are pushing to the tank instead of away. If your pet pushes the mob away from the tank and he doesn’t have firm aggro, the mob will go after whoever does. Also, watch for walls. Non-tank classes attack from the back. If you’ve pushed the mob into a wall, that will take away the ability for them to do that.


## Soloing Tips


If the mob summons, forget it.

If the mob is immune to slow, forget it.

You will almost always want to pull the mob to you with a “slow” spell. A mob that hits hard and fast could spell trouble if he gets to you and resists your first attempt at slowing him. Pulling with slow will buy you time.

Know when to pull off the mob. If you are getting low on health but your pet isn't, let him take a beating for a few. Your pet heals are a lot more efficient then your regular heals. It may not even be necessary to join the fight if it’s possible for you to keep your pet healed. Sit back and gain some mana.


## Raiding Tips


Don’t be afraid to ask your class leader or raid leader what to do. A common mistake is using your MGB up before the encounter. More often than not a raid leader will want you to save that so that you can have it ready to Paragon the raid at the designated time.

Make sure pets are allowed before you summon one. Pets are not always welcome for several reasons. Don’t worry though; you still have more to contribute.
