content:
## Prophecy of Ro


Level range: 50+, with most zones being 60+, and some for well-geared and skilled 70s.

Date of Release: February 21, 2006

The newest expansion, Prophecy of Ro, is doing a couple of interesting things for the game of EverQuest. First of all, this expansion continues the project of revamping the older zones that were lately more like deserted downtowns than a place to stop and stay a while. Freeport and the Deserts of Ro both have gotten extensive graphical updating, while retaining the flavor necessary for nostalgia, "like returning to your hometown after a long absence," as Lead Designer Rashere explained it. New NPCs, new graphics, and more detail that reflects the current state of the game are mixed in with the old favorite places and NPCs. Secondly, the development team has used the idea of time as well as space to expand the world of Norrath, giving us realms from the past as well as new discoveries in the present time. In this expansion, we stay firmly grounded in the original Norrathian world both thematically and in the storyline. This use of past and present to create new adventure zones deepens the understanding of the game world as well as allowing the creation of new zones for adventuring that fit well into the ongoing tale of Norrathian history.

This expansion's story arc follows the tale begun in Depths of Darkhollow with the adventures of the newest deity in the pantheon, Mayong Mistmoore, as well as involving other deities such as Druzzil Ro and Sullon Zek. Mayong has created the Theater of Blood, which the other deities cannot open up, but perhaps mortals can, according to Lead Dev Rashere. There is quite a bit of lore in this expansion, and the new content draws on the classic fantasy genre beloved by EverQuest players. Much of the theme of this expansion seems to concern corruption of power and how it has changed Norrath over the years.

Players can now travel to the past to the forests of Elddar and the ancient elf city, home to the ancestors of the elves. Using the idea of past and present, players can go from the past to the present Ruins of Takish-Hiz, under the sands of the Desert of Ro. Part of this expansion includes an adventure area that is home to the giants of the past, who were intelligent creatures before they were cursed by Rallos Zek during the wars. The giants have all new looks and animations.

Of note is that this expansion is incorporating more NPC actions that are independent of and dependent on player actions in the game, giving it a more realistic feel. More NPCs are interacting in the world, rather than statically standing there waiting for something to happen to them.

By using the device of past and present and what occurs when power corrupts, the design team has immersed players more deeply in the story of the land of Norrath. This expansion features creatively designed zones using older content as well as new, including a tie-in to the lore of the Lost Dungeons of Norrath.

The designers and artists continue to use color and style to give very distinctive flavors to the PoR zones. Using a new tool to design the graphics in the outdoor zones, the design team has given PoR more complex foliage and skylines. EverQuest has evolved into a game where you can expect that the spaces in which you play will be immersive in color, design, and environmental feel reflecting the design team’s ideas.


## Zone Specifics


Revamping of Freeport and the Desert of Ro

The revamping of the older zones is very well done. Freeport is now two zones and contains more content than the older version and is visually stunning. Rashere explained, “Just as the game has grown, so has Freeport.” Now held by both evil and good factions (Sir Lucan was always up to no good), Freeport has the feel of a large port city now and has a much larger area to explore. The underground areas below the streets have also been redone as an adventure zone. Sailing ships are anchored off the docks, giving a much stronger feeling of a harbor than in the original Freeport. The old Theater of the Tranquil now has a large space for PC role playing and has been graphically enhanced to look more like a huge outdoor space for events. The Temple of Marr is much more elaborate, but is still recognizable from the previous version. Outside the city gates, Freeport appears to be a solid city fortress. It is impressive what they have managed to do with one of the first zones ever produced for the game, giving it a fresh new look while keeping the flavor it had previously as a rough seaport town.

The developers understand that many players are kill on site in Freeport, due to the faction hits taken for various reasons, including helping with a paladin quest sword, so there are a number of quests being added to the game designed specifically to raise Freeport faction.

The Deserts of Ro are now two large deserts with much of the old content (yes, the dervs are still there) but with new additions for the expansion. They have fleshed out the details of the landscape and improved the NPC models, bringing these zones up to and even beyond the standards of the newer zones added in later expansions.

Rashere commented that this time "We’ve put an emphasis on quests in the base zones," which can be completed by a single player, but are more likely to need a small group. I asked about solo content, and the basic answer is, EQ is a group-based game so nothing is designed around soloing, but some things can be soloed if you have the gear and the skills to do it.

The Theatre of Blood/Deathknell

For those who liked the old school feeling of the Plane of Fear, and as a warning to those who didn't, the new Theater of Blood is designed to mimic the difficulty and feeling of one of the first additions to the core game. Even the appearance of the zone is much like the old Plane of Fear, pretty in a deadly sort of way, because all of the mobs are difficult, using fearing, spin-stun, and charming abilities. This zone's encounters will be challenging and tough just like the old Plane of Fear was, back when there were 14 hour corpse recoveries and break-ins were as difficult as the core content. Now we have corpse altars so at least you can log out at a decent hour if you wipe, but this zone has been scaled to give the kind of difficult fights players remember but now using better gear, skills, and spells. If you can fight here, the item drops will be worth your while, Rashere hinted.

I have two different stories about who the zone is designed for: one is that mid-range casual guilds will love this zone, and the other is that it's pretty difficult for a group that isn't geared up and well organized, so those types of players may be challenged at a new level. You will just have to go see for yourselves if your guild is up for it. This is a static zone that gives access to the instanced raid zone of Deathknell tower, which means that the old system of competition will be back in the game again. That's old school, too.

Deathknell Tower was built by the goddess of music. The tower is part of a castle, meticulously designed to feature musical elements throughout the zone. The delicate architecture, bejeweled walls, and colorful stained glass windows reflect the feminine personality of the castle's owner. The artists and shaders have outdone themselves with the reflective lighting elements in this structure. Each stained glass window casts colorful prisms of light on the walls and floors. If you see colors on the floor, look up, because they are probably being cast by the stained glass skylight above you. This level of detail is very impressive and adds a great deal of depth to the zone. The musical elements included in the environment are interesting and add flavor to an already complex structure.

That's not to say that you won't die a hideous death inside this beautiful castle. Beware when you gain access through the Theater of Blood and finally climb into the bell tower. The encounters in this zone are very difficult and will require different techniques for defeating it than have been seen in the game previously. Prathun, the zone designer, tells me that he is always looking for new ways to create content that breaks away from traditional encounters and keeps the game fresh. For those guilds that have seen it all, this zone will be something new and a real challenge to defeat.

Plane of Magic

Arcstone, the Isle of Spirits, is the entryway to the Plane of Magic. This zone is about the difficulty of Muramite Proving Grounds, according to the designer. It's sister area above it is the raid zone of Relic, an artifact floating in space created by Druzzil Ro when she experimented with creating life. The first time (and probably the second) you see these towering spires and structures floating in the air, I think you will be impressed with the vision of the design.

The Plane of Magic is shaded in purple with pink flowers and tie-dyed colors, featuring fantastic structures and landscapes that beckon you into the world of wild magic, both natural and controlled. This is Druzzil Ro's world, and although it may be charming, it is home to the remnants of some interesting experiments she performed when making creatures for her Plane that are very aggressive to intruders!

Elddar, the Forest of the Original Elves
Elddar takes you back in time to the ancient world of the elves of Norrath before the different types of elves came to be. This is a static zone for level 70s and is comparable to the Hive in difficulty. PoR takes you from this thriving city and forest to the present time, where the Ruins of Takish-Hiz are now just the remnants of the ancient elvish city, buried under the sands of Ro, part of the entire cursed forest turned into a desert long ago. Takish-Hiz is about the level of Corathus Creep for levels 50 and up and is a static zone as well.

The Plane of Devastation

Quite the opposite of the whimsical and elegant plane of Magic, Devastation is gray and barren as befits a place of anger and suffering. Part of the Plane of Rage, this is home to the Goddess of Rage, Sullon Zek (you may remember meeting her not-so-pleasant brothers in their own planes). This is a place where those that commit murder out of anger are sent when they die. They find themselves a part of the Seething Wall, a mass of living/dead souls awaiting the change to be reborn to fight on in the Devastation and earn the favor of their goddess. They force their way to the forefront of the wall to earn the chance to be called. When they are called to battle by Sullon Zek they fight their way toward the stronghold at the center of the field.

This zone is nothing but barren rock and battle fortifications. This is Sullon Zek's home and unlike Druzzil Ro, she cares nothing for beauty or leisure, only conflict and hatred. In this zone players encounter catapults, which can be destroyed with spells and melee, part of the new feature set for PoR that will allow beating down doors and decimating objects in the game.

This zone has another unique feature: when you die, you don't leave the zone, but instead respawn with your gear back at a spawn point near the wall area. Rashere explains, "Part of the lore behind Devastation is that when someone dies in the war, they go to the writhing wall where they claw their way back to the front over many years and eventually join the war again." This zone is also unqiue because even if players are not in the zone, the npcs are constantly fighting and the zone changes.

This zone should also be popular with kiters because of its huge open spaces.

The Stronghold of Rage is a level 70-geared fortress built by a new race, the Bolvirk, when they were summoned to the Plane of Conflict to aid Sullon Zek after her assention. That was uncounted years ago, and now the Bolvirk no longer remember their once prestigious life in Her service. They battle along with all the rest to control the stronghold. Any army that can control it has a chance to send a member into the tower to serve their goddess. This is the one thing they live for, beyond ruthless destruction.


## New Features: Spheres of Influence and Traps


Two new features are being introduced into the game with this expansion. The first is "spheres of influence" which will create an area of effect. We were shown a lightning storm that struck players and npcs, a display of wild magic that can change magical effects for good or ill. The second is traps, which can be cast and allow players to lure enemies into them for sudden destruction. They were described by Rashere as "pressure points." The trap that we were shown was a three dimensional rune hovering in the air, but they will appear in many different forms when the expansion is released.

Alternate Advancement Although no general AA's a are being introduced into the game this expansion, there will be some AAs that deal specifically with traps and spheres of influence.

Monster Missions There are about 17 new monster missions for those who enjoy a change of pace, and I understand that some of the missions take real skill in tactics to win.

Items and Spells There will be new gear galore, of course, and more higher end droppable gear as well to reflect the growth of the player population. There will be some new spells for level 70s, but this expansion is not about AAs and spells as much as new encounters and new ways to play.

Buff blocker feature Another new addition to the game, should be very helpful to free up player's buff bars for buffs they really need.

This expansion will not include a level increase.

Everything you like about EverQuest --a fantasy based, challenging MMO that is artistically and thematically complex-- is contained in Prophecy of Ro. It has all the elements that players of EQ enjoy. A good story line, zones that are entirely new and visually stunning, challenges for the most jaded players, new gear, and good places to have an adventure is what makes PoR a classic EQ expansion. And you get extra bank slots, new opportunities for tradeskilling, buff blockers, and if you buy the box at retail, a fancy warhorse to ride. For the majority of the playerbase, who are level 50 and above, this expansion should do what it set out to do: provide more challenges, more fun, and something new to explore as well as expand the storyline of Norrath.

## Legends of Norrath


Forsworn, the first expansion set for the popular online strategy game Legends of Norrath™ (LoN), is available for purchase via digital download at www.station.com .

Check out our exclusive art assets and cards from SOE.

“Challenging even the most seasoned strategist, Forsworn presents further opportunities to duel friends and defeat foes with the addition of more than 230 unique cards, several new game mechanics and highly sought after loot items,” said Scott Martins, Director of Development, SOE Denver. “Bringing Legends of Norrath to the international markets of France, Germany and the UK has been a goal for us since the beginning of the development process and we are proud to see that come to fruition.”

Forsworn, the second release in the Legends of Norrath storyline, features enhanced multiplayer support that allows team-based 2 vs. 2 games, as well as cooperative multiplayer “raid” games against powerful AI opponents. Forsworn also boasts 22 additional loot items each for EQ and EQII, including player mounts, potions, clothing and spells and introduces an updated client with new content and bonus features for all registered users.

Available in both 58-card digital starter decks and 15-card digital booster packs, Forsworn cards will be available via digital download only from SOE’s Station Store. The digital starter decks (58 cards) will be available for $9.99USD (plus any applicable taxes), with digital booster packs (15 cards) selling for $2.99USD (plus any applicable taxes).


## Original LoN Review


Legends of Norrath, the EverQuest and EverQuest II based trading card game, is now live and going strong. The game is accessible either by using a tab within both EverQuest games, or by launching the LoN stand-alone client, which can be downloaded from the Legends of Norrath website. Recently I spoke with Paul Dennen, Senior Game Designer for SOE Denver, where the game is produced, about the LoN launch and what players can expect in the future.

With a robust initial card collection of over 375 cards, sophisticated play strategy, and character enhancing loot cards for EverQuest and EverQuestII, LoN is showing itself to be a valuable addition to SOE’s product line. The cards are beautifully illustrated and even the music that accompanies the game is interesting. The card designs all draw on the EverQuest universe, and do not disappoint with the appearance of famous NPC characters, spells, and Norrathian monsters. EQ players will recognize the names some of the currently popular cards for deck builds: "Flowing Black Silk Sash," "Divine Aura," and "Journeyman's Boots." Other cards include the characters Firiona Vie, Lucan D'Vere, and Lord Nagafen.

“Easy to learn, challenging to master” seems to be the design idea for this solid strategy-based game, which provides fun for beginner players as well as challenges in deck building and strategy for hard-core TCG fans. The EverQuest universe gave the LoN developers years of lore and characters to work with for their card designs. “We were given the liberty to come up with our own story,” Dennen said, “so we based [the game play] on a sworn oath to The Tribunal in the Plane of Justice.” According to the official website, the story involves players becoming part of a clandestine war between the forces of Order and Chaos. Jailed on the Plane of Justice, a mysterious tribunal offers the player a chance for freedom and redemption by fighting against the forces of Chaos. By swearing allegiance to the cause of Order, players become Oathbound, and fight secretly to prevent Norrath from plunging into a bloody war.

Legends of Norrath was specifically designed to be a digital trading card game experience, and has elements that make it unique to the TCG genre. For many of these types of games, it’s all about beating up your opponent. LoN certainly follows in the tradition of player beatdown deck builds, but players can also complete lore-driven quests within the game to win, or play a single-player series of scenarios, which add special elements and cards within the game play.

The addition of quest lines are a key element in the game and "add a new kind of victory condition,” Dennen said. Quest lines allow players to employ a different kind of strategy, using tricks and wiles to get around combat.

Adding a further level of complexity, LoN has introduced faction into the card game. Players can choose to use light (good), dark (evil), or neutral cards as they play. Once a faction has been chosen, the player gains various benefits and abilities from using a light or dark card choice. This extra dimension of play adds interest and gives the game an EverQuest feel.

The game's unique elements and depth are a result of a team of strong game designers. Paul Dennen came to the LoN team with years of experience in TCG design. He started his own company, Nayantara Studios, to design and produce Star Chamber, a hybrid of a trading card game and a turn-based strategy game (now distributed by SOE, it’s available in the SOE Station store). He then joined Worlds Apart Productions, the industry leader in digital trading card games. His other TCG titles include Stargate and Auto Assault.

So what makes a good TCG? Dennen gave me some insight into how a successful TCG works. LoN’s cards, like those of other TCGs, are designed to combine simple elements to create an end result greater than its parts. Successful deck builds spawn game turns that “create a synergistic combination,” he said, “surprising your opponent with atomic cards that come together to create powerful effects.” Single effects come on common cards, with effects that are hardest to use appearing on rare cards, making for good balance and sophisticated deck builds.

The innovation of introducing a robust game into an already established MMO was a gamble, but so far seems to have paid off. The addition of loot cards for the EverQuests broke new ground, integrating card playing and MMO, creating a new digital experience players haven’t seen before. The addition of LoN starter decks and loot cards dropping as rare loot in both EQ and EQII promotes the relationship between the two games and has done some interesting things to the economy, with rare loot cards selling for high amounts of platinum in both games.

If a recent tournament stress test is any indication, a lot of people are already playing the game. “We expected maybe hundreds of people to enter the tournament, but when I saw the number of players go over 1000, I just said wow,” Dennen said. There has been some concern from both EQ player bases that the loot cards might unbalance game play, but Dennen reassured me that the loot cards were intended to be cosmetic, not game changing.

The complexity of the game should not deter players of any level of interest to give it a try. Choices in the type of game play are an important component in the design, Dennen said. Legends of Norrath has the depth to satisfy hard core players who expect a TCG to have exciting strategy play with killer card combinations, yet is accessible for the casual player to enjoy an occasional match up in the lobby, he explained. There are single player games, casual games, and more serious tournament challenges. “It’s all about balance,” Dennen said. “It feels cool to be able to have a choice on how to play. You can play the single player game with the scenarios, or try a casual game in the lobby, or work toward a greater understanding of the game and enter tournaments.”

If you are new to the game, start with the Tutorial, now called The Training Grounds, which Dennen pointed out has been greatly improved since the beta, when many EQ and EQII players tried it for the first time. If you found the tutorial a little confusing early on, try it again, he suggested. After you have learned to play, you can head over to the Casual Games Lobby and try out your new skills.

The solo experience consists of challenging encounters with the game's A.I., The Seventh Hammer, or the completion of a set of scenarios. The single player game option is not the primary focus of LoN –- that would be the metagame where players challenge one another -- but does allow players to get their feet wet and start to explore some of the strategic possibilities of the game. By playing the scenarios, players not only learn the game, but gain cards for their decks when they complete their tasks. If you haven’t played TCG games before, the single player option can be a good place to start.

Players can expect another card set to come out in mid-December, just in time for the holidays. This set will continue the theme of the story from Oathbound. Designed as an “expansion,” this set will be smaller than the initial launch set, but will include ten new scenarios. The design team plans on creating more opportunities in the future for cooperative play, so the new set will include more cooperative elements. The idea is to attract a diverse audience of players by offering many ways to enjoy the game.

Legends of Norrath is a great way to try a strategy based card game if you are new to the genre. The barrier to entry is low so it’s easy to start, and with a free deck of cards EverQuest players are good to go. The booster packs are relatively inexpensive if you care to expand your card collection, and the trading lobby is always busy with people exchanging cards. Both for those down-time situations in game and as an entertaining independent game, it appears that LoN is a worthwhile way to spend your time. - Kwill

## Ruins of Kunark


The world of Norrath has expanded with the re-discovery of the continent of Kunark. Races of the light and followers of darkness have set up outposts in this lost world, and adventurers from all over Norrath are arriving daily to explore this vast and untamed land.

Meanwhile, in the center of this dark continent, the Iksar are beginning to expand once again. Isolated for thousands of years, this race of Lizardmen is universally hated by all other races on Norrath. How this introduction of an ancient evil will effect the rest of Norrath is yet to be seen...

IGN’s EverQuest Vault has opened up their Guidebook to Kunark. In this constantly updated guide, you will find detailed role-playing strategies, maps of zones, as well as strategy from other experienced players.

## The Scars of Velious


The world of Norrath has expanded once again with the re-discovery of the continent of Velious. The crafty little Gnomes of Norrath have set up a small outpost on this lost world, and adventurers from all over Norrath are arriving daily to explore this vast and untamed land.

Meanwhile, in the center of this frozen continent, three races wage an ancient war. Isolated for thousands of years, the Dragons, Storm Giants, and Coldain Dwarves don't know how to trust other races on Norrath. How this introduction of a new continent will effect the rest of Norrath is yet to be seen...

IGN’s EverQuest Vault has opened up their Guidebook to Velious. The guide is still very new, and only contains some basic zone and moster information, as well as the backstory at this moment.

content:
## PC Cheats


This page contains a list of cheats, codes, Easter eggs, tips, and other secrets for EverQuest for PC . If you've discovered a cheat you'd like to add to the page, or have a correction, please click EDIT and add it .


## Good Exp for low levels in Qeynos Area


You must be in qeynos area before ateempting this trick, and around lvl 2-4. Once you reach level 3, go to Qeynos hills and kill Gnolls, Gnoll pups , Gnoll scouts or Gnoll watchers. There is a slight chance they will drop gnoll fangs. Get 4 (or more) gnoll fangs and take them to the captain of the gaurds that overlooks the arena. Give him 4 teeth at a time. He will give you lots of exp and 4 moonstones. Give the moonstones to the bartender in the back of the bar in South Qqeynos. He will also give you exp.


## Good Exp for Levels 11 to 14 in Qeynos Hills


Go to Qeynos Hills and hunt down Rabid Grizzleys. They are about level 12 to 14. Kill them (while keeping an eye out for Cros or Holly who will kill you for attacking animals), then loot the rabid pelt off them. Take the pelt to the UFO in North Qeynos and hand them into the Priestess wearing leather. You will get VERY good exp, 1 to 2pp and a spell (usually endure disease).

## Game Basics



## Game Basics


EverQuest is a "Massively Multiplayer Online  		  Roleplaying Game". In it, you take the role of an adventurer and set out  		  to make your mark on the World of Norrath.

You are able to choose from multiple races  		  including:

Human

Half Elf

High Elf

Wood Elf

Dark Elf

Barbarian

Eurdite

Dwarf

Halfling

Gnome

Troll

Ogre

As well as many Classes:

Warrior

Ranger

Paladin

Shadowknight

Wizard

Enchanter

Necromancer

Magician

Druid

Cleric

Monk

Rogue

Shaman

This guide will use many terms that may be unfamiliar to people who have  		  not played EverQuest before. Here is a short list of some of the terms that  		  will be used in this guide:

Mob : Another  		      term for monster, spawn, etc.

Spawn: When mob "appears" in EverQuest,  		      it is considered a spawn. For example, if a camp full of Orcs is replenishing  		      itself slowly, it is having a slow spawn.

Cp: Copper Pieces, the lowest form of  		      currency.

Sp: Silver Pieces.

Gp: Gold Pieces

Pp: Platinum Pieces, the highest form  		      of currency.

Train: When someone is fighting a mob,  		      and gets in a little over their head, they may run. Many mobs will help each  		      other out, so if one sees another one running, he will join in on the fun.  		      This has a snowball effect where mobs will continue to be added to the line,  		      forming a Train. These usually head directly to the zone. In some areas,  		      such as Unrest, Mistmoore, Sol A and B, and Cazic Thule when you hear shouts  		      of "Train" run to the zone line as fast as you can (or gate out if you are  		      a caster).

Zone: Areas in EverQuest are called "zones".  		      Each of these have "zone lines" that load up the next zone when you cross  		      them.

Exp: Short for experience.

Yard Trash: This is a term for wandering  		      mobs in a certain area. For example, the bugs and low level undead in the  		      area surrounding the house in Unrest are considered "Yard Trash".

Camp/Camping: To sit in one spot to kill  		      a specific mob.

Drop: Another term for what a mob has  		      in terms of loot.

Nuke: To blast a target with spells.
